candidates.review_text: I've been to this place a couple of times with a group of people and in general thought it was good. I definitely enjoy going back, however I've had mixed experiences with the spice level. The menu is helpful because it indicates the spice level of each meal, although the lowest is three, I think. Definitely could make more dishes that appeal to those of us that don't like spicy. The first time I went I got a meal that was advertised as three (to them not spicy) and asked for no peppers and mild. It came out perfect and I loved it. However the next time the waitress seemed annoyed and it came out spicier. That is my only complaint, so for those who need mild dishes, just be adamant and careful about it. However, overall great food and I will definitely be going back!

Fantastic experience!! 

I am NOT a spice person and this place is known for its spicy cuisine. I had help from our great waiter to pick items that weren't too spicy and I was golden so know that if you don't do spicy you can still go here! And you should!!! They give their items a rating from 1-10 for spiciness, 10 being the most spicy. I would suggest if you can't handle spice definitely stick to anything less than a 3! 

Highly suggest getting a reservation if you can. This place is always packed and always a wait. We had a reservation for three people and were seated immediately. 

Served family style but can get individual meals- but everything is large portions and greatly priced. Great bang for your buck. All of the food comes out when it's ready so you just kind of wait and anticipate things to come out whenever it's ready. 

Amazing experience. Definitely go! And whatever you get, make sure one of the items is the pork buns!

I like everything I've had at Ekta except the Ekta vegetables. They are mostly just bell peppers and mine came with two chunks of paneer cheese in it even though it's not listed as an ingredient on the menu. I won't be ordering that again. My boyfriend gets the tandoori chicken and loves it.  We've tried several dishes that were all very good, as well. They give you plenty of rice, but naan costs extra. They opt for the weird sesame crackers as their free appetizer. I'm not a fan of them, but I always eat them anyway.

This place has pretty decent ambiance. It's quiet and classy, and also BYOB. The service is reserved, but absolutely adequate and polite. Street parking can be sketchy, but fortunately we live locally and are able to walk. There are plenty of cabs nearby, as well. 

The one thing I would like from Ekta is the option to select the spice level of my dishes. Their menu is set up so that most dishes are not spicy at all, and a few are slightly spicy.  I like my Indian food tongue-stingingly spicy and I have never been to an Indian restaurant that didn't ask what my preference was. If they had this, I would give them five stars.

I like this place. The atmosphere is nice and bright in the back dining room. It is like a greenhouse almost. 

Ordering through yelp was easy. Pickup was super easy. Glad I ordered mild b c it was still pleasantly spicy. But not too much.

This place was a nice surprise.  We thought it might be too spicy, but we lucked out and ordered some items that brought some heat, but didn't leave us going down in flames.  Loses a star as our wonderful waiter was overwhelmed with two tables of 14 people and us.  Certainly NOT his fault, but he simply could not keep up with bringing drinks, appetizers, soups, and main meals out to 30 people all at the same time.  I have to think someone took the reservation for these tables, so they could have used another server.  But let's talk about what we had here, because it was fantastic and I would go back again in a 28 Spice Hot Minute!  Started with a Dragon Nectar cocktail that was on the Happy Hour menu.  It's one of those drinks that tastes so good you don't realize you are getting hammered while sipping away on this delicious concoction.  Appetizers - we tried the Rock Shrimp - it has some sort of aioli sauce on it that was highly addicting.  For soup, I chose the Tom Yum Soup with chicken - I don't know who Tom is but it was indeed Yummy!  We split two entrees - the Saigon Beef - which there was nothing left on the plate of that item and the Hot Sauce Style Szechuan Chicken - you can choose the fire level on this and we took it down ONE FIRE emblem and that was perfect for us.  This comes in more of a soup bowl with lots of sauce, so although we made it through all the protein with this offering, there was a lot of extra sauce left.  Had to wait a long time for our check due to the 28 other guests at two tables, but we weren't catching a train, so we were fine just chatting until we finally got checked out.  It's on my list to come back and try other things on the menu.

I am not really a fan of cheesesteaks, but I want one a couple of times a year. Today was one of those days and now I may crave one more often, thanks to Cleavers. 

For some reason, that I can't think of I've never tried Cleavers before. But, today, I ordered through Door Dash. I got MYO Ribeye on seeded roll, with mild provolone, fried Onions, cherry pepper relish, and portobello mushrooms. The only reason I gave four stars was that the cherry pepper relish was a bit too spicy for my taste, but it easily could have been five stars. The sandwich was huge (1/2 is in my refrigerator for tomorrow), the onions and mushrooms were cooked perfectly. (I hate so- called fried onions that are partially raw and crunchy) and the roll was perfect. It was nice not having a cotton textured Amaroso roll! 

I also enjoyed the strawberry cheesecake.

UPDATE, I reheated the remaining half for lunch today and the cherry pepper relish got even hotter. I took one bite and couldn't eat it.  Usually, I like food that is somewhat hot, but this was extreme IMO. This is not a criticism, just a warning. Unless you like very hot food, skip the relish. My mouth still hurts a half hour later.

Went with high expectations. To preface, I enjoy spicy food. Ordered a gin cocktail with the Thai chili and it was spicy, but tolerable (I would recommend it). For my entree, I ordered the pad see ew with mild spice. I couldn't eat more than a few bites because my mouth was on fire. Our waitress (Hanna) picked up on the fact that I barely touched the food and asked if everything was okay. I explained that it was too spicy for me personally and she took it back and brought me a new plate with no spice. Great service, good food, and I felt comfortable eating here with the Covid pandemic. They followed a good process. Highly recommended.

Went there to have a dinner with my gf yesterday, and ordered quiet lot of food, we love spicy very much. And i asked the waitress to add more spicy on some of my food, but it came out not too spicy but its an ok. But overall was excelent. Still want to come and to make sure make it more more spicy :)

I really like this place. The food is saucy with the numbing kind of spiciness. However, the numbing isn't overpowering and goes really well with the dishes. I'm really particular about how spicy dishes are and this place does it well. It's spicy, but not too spicy you can't enjoy your food.

Food comes out fast and service is good. Definitley come in a group and do family style as you'll be able to try a whole variety of food.

Added benefit is they're never too crazy busy and have plenty of seating to fit larger groups. 

Tip: Don't drink water right away after eating the dumbing spice ;)

First time ordering, will definitely be back! I got the kua kling curry, and it was amazing, but fair warning, they are not kidding when they say it's VERY hot. I love spicy food and it was a perfect spice level for me, but it is certainly not for the faint of heart

Don't get me wrong, the food here is great. Everything is extremely well prepared and flavorful. The waitstaff was accommodating to our mix of palates (2 children and a vegetarian) and offered to adjust the spice level or bring the sauces on the side to ensure no one was overwhelmed with something too spicy.

The only reason it doesn't get 5 stars is that everything was salty beyond what would be considered reasonable, IMO. Sure, this amplified the flavor, but everyone also felt the need to drink a quart of water on the way home to balance out their sodium levels.

The heat levels were about what you'd expect. A "4 dot" dish (which translates to "Hot") is pretty spicy but not nose running, drooling, lips on fire hot. You'll actually be able to taste your food.

Amazing hot pot. The best I've had in Chinatown. Really fresh ingredients all around - we got both the beef combo and the seafood combo, and was impressed by the quality. The seafood platter even came out with an ice sculpture! Maybe a bit over the top, but still a nice touch.

We also ordered two servings of the noodles - very colorful, I think the flavors were purple yam, a vegetable one, and something else. We ordered a couple more things and the bill came to $50/pp ($200 total including tip, split between 4 people). To be honest I could have probably eaten a lot more because the food was so yummy, but we wanted bubble tea for dessert so I disciplined myself to stop. Plus, $50/pp is not cheap when the other hot pot we've had before averaged around $30/pp.

Our waitress was very helpful in giving us guidance on what to order, and kept us updated on the progress of our food coming out if we had been waiting for awhile. We ordered the heaven/hell hot pot with the tomato oxtail broth and the entry-level spicy (not spicy at all in my opinion but the 3 friends I was with said it was spicy enough for them). Our friends at the other table ordered the medium-level spicy and they said their mouths were burning, lol. 

My mouth is watering as I'm recalling our experience and how delicious all the food was. The price is worth the experience and quality of food.

TLDR: Good pho, lively atmosphere, but not spicy enough.

I went with some family friends who are Vietnamese food experts (aka they are from vietnam and their mission in life is to hit up every pho place), so I deferred to their judgement. We ordered a platter type dish (quiche, pork, rice, veggies), chicken pho, spring rolls, and Bun Bo Hue, a spicy beef soup. I was really excited about the Bun Bo Hue, because I rarely see spicy items at Vietnamese places (although there is plenty of sriracha and chili jam-type condiments to add), but there was ZERO heat in the soup. If someone told me that this item was meant to be spicy, I wouldn't have believed them. It was less spicy than mild salsa. It was delicious, but not spicy. 

I appreciate the plant-filled decor (I'm a sucker for plant life), and this place was packed 45 minutes from closing time, so clearly it's popular. The staff are nice and friendly, but they did forget my request to not add cilantro to my dish, so points off for that. My friends were satisfied with their dishes, and the portions were very generous.

Overall, it was a great place, and I would go there again if I were in the area.

Really delicious meal, but be careful about the spice level you ask for. I usually have a high spice tolerance, and I have never found anything "too spicy", so coming here, when they asked for the spice level that I wanted, I was too cocky. They gave me the options from 1-10, or an 11 if I really wanted it spicy. I chose to get an 11 for my crispy Fried chicken wings, and it was way way too spicy.

The chicken was covered in chili seeds. It was delicious, but after two wings, it was a very painful kind of delicious.

I went here with a friend and we did the All You Can Eat Hot Pot. They had a wide selection of food but I wish the meat category had more options. Nonetheless, what we ordered was still very delicious. We got the spicy broth and it was very flavorful, a bit too spicy for me but still enjoyable. I definitely would recommend this place and will be returning!

Came here on a late Sunday afternoon looking for a table for 2 and had to wait 20 minutes. 

We both ordered the spicy ramen. I really liked that you could chose the saltiness and the way the noodles are cooked. 

The pork was soooo tasty! I would definitely recommend that. 

Let me preface this next part with saying that I really enjoy spicy foods but this was way too spicy for me!!! I couldn't really enjoy the flavor that much because it was that spicy!!


So buyers beware - when they say spicy they mean it!

I think I may have finally found my favorite dan dan noodles in the city!

Came here on Saturday night with my sister and boyfriend after an afternoon of shopping. I remembered reading about this place in a recent article about the best new restaurants in the city, so when we passed it by we decided to try it out.
 
The ambiance was modern, open and bright. It was pretty crowded but we managed to snag some bar seats and ordered a round of drinks. Drinks were decent, a tad on the sweet side but we still enjoyed them. We also put in an order of the Dan Dan noodles. 

I have to say, I don't handle spice all that well to begin with. Unfortunately for me, dan dan noodles tend to be on the spicy side and up until this point I haven't been able to find the perfect balance between spicy and sweet. Dan Dan definitely found that balance for me! They were not too spicy, perfectly cooked noodles and I was able to taste the peanut sauce without being overwhelmed with heat.

I will definitely be back to try the other menu items!

MOMMY!

The spice level here is ridiculous.  I don't think I am a lightweight but these folks DO NOT MESS AROUND.  You've got to be honest about your spice intake level because it will be super spicy even if you say "not too spicy".  

I couldn't finish the Dan Dan Noodles I ordered.  It looked awesome though.  I took one bite and DAM, everything was all of a sudden really hot.  I wanted to yank out my digestive track because I felt the burn all the way down.  The dry pot fish which came later also looked awesome and was equally spicy as well!  I drank like 4 glasses of water in like 10 mins.  I honestly couldn't doggie bag my leftovers fast enough to leave and get more liquids ASAP.  

The people behind the counter were super friendly and made solid recommendations.  They also brought my food to my table and refilled my water glass quickly.  Perhaps sensing that I was probably going to spew fire from my mouth and burn the whole place down.  Aside from the extreme heat, I did like the food and hope to revisit soon, with extra fire extinguishers for my mouth.

We found the food to be too spicy to be able to taste the other flavors.  Everyone in my group arrived thinking we enjoyed spicy food.  Apparently we do not.  We ordered only dishes that had mid-level heat ratings (4-6) and found that with only one exception the flavors were overpowered by the chilies.  
The \dish we most enjoyed were the dan dan noodles.
So,if everyone in your group likes really, really hot food this is the place for you.

It was way too spicy for me. I literally had stomach pains for the next two days. If you like spicy, then go for it. If you can only eat traditionally spicy (the kind you can control yourself, i.e on the side etc), avoid it.

Ok - I like spicy (scotch bonnet, Tabasco, jalapeño, cayenne).  My daughter does not.  We ordered mild.  The food was incredibly spicy.  Too spicy.  Way too spicy.  would not order from here again even though they offered us a credit.

Never do I really write reviews but I feel like I had to this time around. My boyfriend & I come to this place very often, we really loved this place. The most recent time we brought my mom, who's an occasional Mexican food eater. We ordered food that was too spicy for her and spicier than normal for us (her first bit she was choking, eyes watering, gulping water, etc.). We called the server over and asked her if we could exchange for no spicy sauce. Really nice server told us she didn't think so but she'll ask her manager -- came back and she said that her manager told her that we have to purchase another one without spicy sauce + get charged for the plate we cannot eat. I was surprised so I asked to speak to the manager myself! The manager in a rude tone told me the same thing but then also began to tell me that, "We lose a lot of money for people sending food back... we can fire up another one but you're going to have to pay for both... because this is how you ordered your food". Unheard of! Moral of the story -- you better enjoy what you get at this place or ask for a glass of milk if it's too spicy, because if not... you have to purchase another order so they don't "lose money".

for the most part I thought it was pretty good, I wish the made the danger pie less spicy, I didn't mind but my kids thought it was too spicy(so make a pie more for kids).
the waiters and servers need to learn a bit more etiquette, they were handling the food over our heads, with hot food and kids thats not a very good practice. I hope they read this.

Asked if the chorizo was spicy because I needed to order something for my son. She said no. We get it. Not only is it spicy, it came with extra hot sauce on the plate. When I told them it was too spicy,  she said there's nothing I can do about that.  Add that to the fact they only take cash in 2016, I am really disappointed. Oh and the rice and beans didn't come out with our meal and the chips and pico took so long, we got it to go. A smile and hello when you enter a business would be nice.

Came here for a dinner with a friend - I've heard of this place many times but have never tried it so I was really excited. I arrived at Zaika before my friend and even though there were 2 occupied tables - it was VERY QUIET. Even after my friend came, it still was quiet to the point we were whispering which felt really awkward. 

Our waiter was nice and I asked him about spicy dish recommendations he had and he told me to get the chicken karahi, which he said was the spiciest. However when I got the entree, it was not spicy AT ALL and I was disappointed. Don't get me wrong, it was still good but it would have been perfect if it was spicy. When I told him it wasn't spicy, he said he made it a medium because he thought it would be too spicy for me. I was irritated when he said this because I can determine what spice level I want without him deciding for me. The cheese naan was really tasty and so was the mango lassi. 

While we were eating, the two other tables left but they were not cleaned for our entire dinner! They had to have left at least 30-45 minutes before we did. By the time we left, a huge party left as well - so that's 4 tables he had to clean and it seemed like there was only one waiter. 

The only good thing was that they had a nice Zaika pen to sign our receipts with which he let me keep but I'm not sure if I would come back here even though the food was good.

Long wait time for outside seating. Food was OK. WAY TOO SPICY. Not able to enjoy due to food being way to spicy. 
Waitress too busy. Very friendly but way too busy.

So sad I have to write this negative review. Especially since I gave a perfect review before and would frequent this place at least once a week. I'm not sure if they have new owners but the food has definitely changed, for the worst! I would call and most likely get the same things. They would know who I was when I called or whenever I picked my food up. The last few months haven't been that way. I ordered a dish I always ordered. It's a little spicy but not too much to handle. The last TWO times I ordered it (singapore mei fun) it has been so spicy I couldn't eat one bite without a drink followed behind. No lie! Ordered a chicken & broccoli w garlic sauce (this dish is never spicy here) that too was fire beyond belief. I did id call and let them know they "apologized" I let it go. Ordered the same thing another day this time I did tell them not too spicy. Of course it was just as FIRE as the first time. Also didn't deliver everything that I paid for. Then to top it off was a bug in my food. I was done after that and haven't been back since. 

This place use to be my spot now it's just NOT!

To be honest, if you want authentic Sichuan hot pot, then you might not want to come here. The only good thing I'd say about this place is that the meat quality is decent; however, nothing else meets our expectations. We ordered extra spicy soup base, but it's not spicy at all, only a thin layer of chili oil floating on the top. I think the chili sauce from the sauce tray might even be spicier than the soup base, very disappointing. The service was okay, they never added the soup for us unless we asked them to do. But the most frustrating thing was that when we wanted to chat and stay for a bit after we paid the check, the waitresses just kept staring and looking at us like they wanted us to leave immediately. I don't think this is how customers should be treated here.

We went there with high expectation but boy o boy, was it awful... first they gave us a big table, after that they served us our bonchon and drinks. Then the host informed us that she "forgot" this big table was reserved for someone else, so we have to move!!! How on earth you can't remember you have a reservation??? So they moved us to a smaller table... we ordered hotpot for one of our friend and both BBQ and hotpot for two of us... the server was soooo unhelpful we had to ask him everything... he could clearly understand that we are struggling, still he just stood there like a duck... then food arrived... Two of us chose spicy soup base... if you are reading this review please DO NOT order this... it comes in a pot which is filled with oil and  LOTS of spices (whole black pepper, cloves, star anise and red chili )... and not spicy at all, it just tastes oily... the kimchi soup base was ok...  for BBQ we chose marinated beef short rib and sirloin... nothing exceptional... will I ever go back? HELL NO!!! So disappointed!!!
We placed the order for sweet sour fish(supposedly not spicy) it turned out very spicy. We asked for not spicy, that's what we got. Thank you so much to ruin my day !!!!!!!

Horrible. I am on Immunotherapy treatment for cancer and spicy food can make my stomach feel terrible. For a treat I entered, ordered and waited for a take-out of a supposedly mild dish (Baingan Bhurta) and was reassured of this by the waiter. I read Indian food is good for cancer and have had very mild and delicious Indian food in the past. Got home and just one mouth full was spicy hot and immediately spit it out. Took me tons of water and milk to get the "spicy" feel out of my mouth. I called them furious and asked for a refund, told them I had been REASSURED this was a mild dish, that I was on a cancer drug. They argued the dish was not spicy and would not offer a refund. In addition, they were rude and abrupt.

There are few restaurants that lead me to write reviews, but such a poor dining experience has led me to put pen to paper so to speak. The ambience of the restaurant is good and the restaurant is accommodating to children. The appetizers of a wonton chicken soup, Chinese broccoli and veggie spring rolls were all pretty good.
However, the entrées were very bad. We ordered spicy lemongrass soup. The soup was not spicy and worse, the chicken was bland. Upon asking the waiter about the soup he said it "was not spicy" despite spicy being in THE NAME of the dish. When we asked the waiter to take the dish back, he did so quickly and did not ask if we would prefer another or if he could do anything to help. We also had beef dishes that were better, but still bland. I recommend searching for another place to dine if flavor is your prerogative for the evening.

We order from here very frequently, and the food is usually very good, however it can be very inconsistent depending on the chef. We just ordered the red curry, "spice level 3" (whatever that means), which we've gotten plenty of times in the past. It's usually honestly not spicy enough, however today it had both myself and my girlfriend in tears (and we both love spicy food), and was basically inedible. Pattaya needs to figure out how to prepare food consistently, but until then, ordering I'd a huge gamble.

I met some friends here; as my friends raved about this place and it was Univ. Dining Days.  So there were two couples and a 2 year old at the table.  We ordered.  10 minutes later I got my entree but nobody else got theirs.  Then another 5 minutes later (I started eating already) waiter came out and said they were out of a key ingredient for the other 3 entrees; did we want to order something else?  We said send us a manager.  He was nice and took another order and they gave us all the later entrees for no charge.  But the food was pretty greasy and barely edible ; My wife took 3 bites and didn't even ask to take the rest home.  My Pad Thai was OK, but was not spicy at all despite being labelled as spicy on the menu.     and i had to take our 2 year old to run up and down the Sheridan elevator to entertain him while everyone else finished eating.  The one star is for the fact they acknowledged their error and made good on it.  But the food was no worth the price in any event.  My wife was hungry when she got home.

I asked for a suggestion from the server for something spicy and I ordered what they suggested. It was not spicy and full of tomato sauce which I don't like. When I asked if it was possible to swap the dish for something else the manager came over and complained that this is the most famous dish we have and everyone likes it. I would've been fine with just hearing that it's not our policy or something but the way they handled it was rude and unprofessional. I tried to ask a follow up questions and the manager just said no no no we cannot change it.
We were celebrating my friend getting a fellowship they really wanted and this was such a bummer. We left the food as is, paid the bill and got out. Never going there again.

For the kinds of restaurants that occupy 44th Street, Tampopo is painfully average. The place does not offer anything that you can't find at Koreana or Chattime closer to campus, and at lower prices.

I ordered a spicy beef bowl here, and was pleasantly surprised by the portions. Unfortunately, the positives ended there. The dish was both too salty and too spicy, and I take spice just fine. Just the mixture of the sodium and spice compounded to pummel my mouth, which was not a pleasant feeling. It didn't help that there was all of three florets of broccoli, not nearly enough vegetables to balance out the beef and rice.

I rarely venture out to 44th Street as is for food. Now, outside of Honest Tom's or Lil Pop Shop next door, I may not be back anytime soon.

}
